welcomeToAddis.headline: A city of history, conversation, coffee, and constant discovery
welcomeToAddis.editorialIntro: Addis Ababa is best explored with context. One street can lead from a national museum to a busy market, a historic cathedral, a contemporary gallery, or a quiet coffee stop. Addis Ababa by Locals brings these experiences together, helping you decide what to see, how to get there, and which local services fit your visit.

addisHighlights.headline: Must-Sees in Addis Ababa
addisHighlights.subheadline: Start with the places that reveal Addis Ababa's history, daily life, faith, art, and mountain views.

attractions.title: National Museum of Ethiopia
attractions.description: Home to Lucy, the 3.2-million-year-old hominid fossil. Recently renovated with improved exhibits.

attractions.title: Addis Mercato (Merkato)
attractions.description: Africa's largest open-air market with over 13,000 vendors selling spices, textiles, and coffee.

attractions.title: Holy Trinity Cathedral
attractions.description: Architectural masterpiece and final resting place of Emperor Haile Selassie.

attractions.title: Entoto Park
attractions.description: Panoramic city views from Addis Ababa's highest point at 3,200 meters.

columns.title: Visa & Entry
columns.description: Most nationalities require a visa (available on arrival or e-visa). Check requirements before travel.

columns.title: Best Time to Visit
columns.description: October to March (dry season, mild temperatures). Peak season November–February with major festivals.

columns.title: Currency & Payments
columns.description: Ethiopian Birr (ETB). ATMs widely available. Credit cards accepted at major hotels and restaurants.

columns.title: Altitude & Health
columns.description: Addis Ababa sits at 2,400 meters. Take it easy on your first day, stay hydrated.
